text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Toyota Motor Corp Australia has had a loss of A$53 million for 1996 on its car manufacturing and importing operations, with the company losing a large amount at the new Altona plant. Australia's market has seen Toyota and Mitsubishi suffer heavy losses, while Ford and General Motors have had good profits. Page 21.

BHP Copper chief executive Jim Lewis has acted on a threat made earlier this year to slash costs inside some of its United States copper mines, with 630 jobs likely to be lost at the high-cost Pinto Valley mine and another 500 job likely to be cut from the ageing San Manuel mine. Page 21.

As part of its plan to become a major iron ore producer in its own right, Hancock Prospecting Ltd, the company of the late Lang Hancock, announced two key appointments yesterday and confirmed a partial float is being considered. Liberal Party powerbrkers and corporate consultants Michael Kroger and Michael Yabsley have been appointed to two subsidiary boards. Page 21.

Shell Co of Australia chief executive Roland Williams believes the future of the Australian coal industry is uncertain unless the threat of competition from Asia is countered. Williams says the competition in the sector is increasing, and believes the log-term potential in New South Wales is "good". Page 23.
THE AUSTRALIAN

WD & HO Wills Holdings Ltd is suing rival Phillip Morris Australia in the Federal Court for deceptive and misleading conduct. Wills claims Morris' new brand, Summit, is a direct take-off of its own brand, Horizon. Wills says Phillip Morris is in breach of the Trade Practices Act, and would undercut the value-for-money price range. Page 29.

Former Reserve Bank deputy governor John Phillips has labelled a plan to see a mega regulator overseeing Australia's financial system as "frightening". Phillips says a regulator, as proposed by the Wallis report inquiry into the financial system, would have a "real tendency to become excessively bureaucratic and more and more distant". Page 31.

CanWest chairman Izzy Asper has met with "six or seven" of the dozen potential buyers of the 18.5 percent stake of Ten Group Ltd that must be sold by CanWest by September 30. Federal Treasurer Peter Costello has ordered two companies financed by CanWest to sell their interests to ensure they do not breach foreign ownership regulations. Page 31.

Junior miner Goldminco NL has signed Paladin Resources NL for four uranium exploration licenses in South Australia. The announcement comes amid continued activity in the uranium market, with world supplies down and Australia's deposits open to further exloration. Page 33.

Pasminco executive director for mining Bryan Davis says current exploration projects could lead to a resurrection of the zinc and lead industry in New South Wales. Davis says new discoveries are expected in the Broken Hill region, through the state goverment's Discovery 2000 programme. Page 33.

Sipa Resources International NL has extended its bid for Arcadia Resources NL, but Sipa directors believes the company is unlikely to secure control. Sipa is looking to consolidate ownership of a project in Western Australia and is unsure of Arcadia's interests, although its bid being found fair and reasonable by independent valuers Minval Associates. Page 33.

RTZ-CRA is examining the iron carbide method of downstream iron ore processing as a potential alternative to its current A$300 million HIsmelt pilot project. The mining giant is said to be closely watching the progress of an iron carbide plant in Jamaica operated by giant U.S. steel manufacturer Nucor NUE.AX. Page 30.

The Australian Gas Association has warned that delays to gas reform could jeopardise A$14 billion worth of investment in major energy projects planned for the next decade. The comments come in a major study to be released by the AGA today at a gas industry conference in Canberra. Page 30.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Goodman Fielder has hired three senior staff from rival Burns Philp as speculation mounts Goodman will bid to take over the troubled company. Goodman chairman David Clarke confirmed the new appointments, but denied to comment on high-level meetings between the two companies or his company's purchase of Burns shares. Page 37.

The Corporate Directors' Association of Australia is concerned about the large amounts of stock bought by Colonial board members and senior management when other parties only received small amounts of stock. Association executive director Chris Peters says shareholders have a reasonable argument to say they were disadvantaged. Page 37.

The sharemarket is predicted to reach unprecedented heights this week, bolstered by strong gains in the U.S. sharemarket and last week's interest rate cut. On Friday there was a 87.78 point gain in the Dow Jones Industrial Average index to 7345.91 points, eclipsing Thursday's record close of 7333.55. Page 39.

Calls by the Foreign Investment Review Board that French insurer Axa-UAP concede ownership of its planned Chinese life insurance venture to its Australian unit, have been rejected. Axa-UAP says that as it has been granted permission by Chinese authorities to sell life insurance in China, it would do so and said the decision did not harm Australian interests. Page 39.

Former Reserve Bank deputy governor John Phillips has criticised the Wallis report's recommendation for a mega-regulator of the financial system. Phillips says the report's argument for separation of monetary policy from Reserve Bank supervision was "not compelling". Page 39.

Gina Rinehart has enlisted the support of two influential Liberal Party figures, former Victorian Liberal Party president Michael Kroger and former New South Wales Tourism Minister Michael Yabsley, to help establish Hancock Prospecting as a leading iron ore producer at its Hope Downs project in the Pilbara. The two have recently jointed the boards of Hancock Prospecting units Hope Downs and Hancock Minerals. Page 39.
THE AGE

There is speculation Goodman Fielder may bid for food group Burns Philp & Co after the former was successful in gaining three senior executives from Burns. Goodman is expected to acquire Burns Philp's global yeast business after the company took serious losses from its move into herbs and spices. Page B1.

The amounts of stock given to Colonial board members and senior management has been criticised by financial institutions and shareholder lobby groups. The Corporate Directors Association of Australia believes the deals raise questions of corporate governance. Page B1.

Pharmaceutical cooperative Amcal has launched a retail strategy to boost sales and maintain market share in light of a possibility that supermarkets could sell drugs from 1999. Under the plan, all Amcal chemists will be required to install new signage within two years and remodel their stores within five years. Page B1.

Coplex Resources NL, the Hobart-based but internationally focused oil and gas group, has launched a new corporate strategy to make it more attractive to Australian investors and raise its market price from the current 33 cents a share. Coplex will focus on building up overseas interests into three core Canadian-listed subsidiaries. Page B3.

Cathay Pacific Airways suspended a fifth of its fleet and 15 flights yesterday after concerns about the safety of it Rolls-Royce engines were expressed to it by Rolls-Royce. Hong Kong's Dragonair has suspended a similar number of airplanes and flights for the same reason. Page B1.

Since becoming managing director of Melbourne-based design and engineering firm E.W. Cox in 1990, Hartmut Hofmann has transformed the company into a leading supplier of building maintenance equipment in Australia and Asia. He claims his rigorous restructuring programme introduced an export-oriented culture to the company. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
